agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Sets rules for collecting, processing, disclosing and transferring personal data, granting data subjects rights and imposing duties on controllers and processors. Applies in the Kingdom and to residents' data processed abroad. Enforced by a Competent Authority with fines and criminal penalties. Effective 720 days after publication.
summary.long: The Law regulates collecting, processing, disclosing, transferring and destroying personal data in the Kingdom and residents' data processed abroad, excluding purely personal or family use. Data subjects gain rights to be informed, access and obtain their data, correct it and request its destruction. Processing generally requires consent, subject to listed exceptions including legitimate interest, which does not cover sensitive data. Controllers must limit purpose and content, provide a privacy policy and notice at collection, restrict disclosure, implement security measures and notify breaches. Health data, credit data, marketing communications and research uses have specific conditions. Controllers must carry out impact assessments for products or services and keep processing records. Cross-border transfers require a listed purpose and an adequacy assessment by the Competent Authority. The Competent Authority supervises compliance, may keep a national register of controllers, and may license accreditation and audit bodies. Intentional disclosure of sensitive data for harm or personal benefit carries up to two years' imprisonment and/or a three-million-riyal fine; other violations carry warnings or fines up to five million riyals. Courts may order confiscation and publication of judgments, and individuals may claim compensation. The Law takes effect 720 days after publication.

notes: Annotated from the English translation supplied; quotes are verbatim from it. The text contains no Royal Decree number or date and no amendment; registry metadata cites Royal Decree M/19 and amendment M/148, which the text does not reflect. The Implementing Regulations are not included. Article 32 is repealed. Art. 29(4) refers to subparagraphs (b) and (c) of Art. 29(2), which the text letters A to C. The Art. 36(2) committee and Art. 37 inspectors are appointed by decision of the Competent Authority president and are not named bodies.
